source.head: feature/enforce-document-birth-info
source.title: BirthInfo (NestJS): KYC birth info must match the identity document
source.intent:
BirthInfo: enforce document birth info on KYC submissions
POST /users/:userId/birth-info now rejects (422) a submission that contradicts
the user's identity document. Each part the document has (country of birth,
place of birth) must match; a part extraction couldn't read is not enforced,
and with no document data at all the user's answer is saved as before. The
submission still overwrites the previous KYC birth info.

Save the KYC birth info and its event in one transaction

cases.label: POST /users/u-2/birth-info IND/Mumbai (country matches, document has no place)
POST /users/u-4/birth-info nga/lagos (place matches, document has no country)

BirthInfoVerifier.summary: Holds what a user submits in KYC to their identity document: every part the document has must match. A part the document is missing (extraction couldn't read it) is not enforced, and with no document data at all the user's answer stands, as it always did.

diff.text: verify(submitted: KycBirthInfoDto, document: BirthPlace | null): BirthInfoVerification {
if (!document) return { ok: true, enforced: [], mismatches: [] };
const enforced = FIELDS.filter((f) => document[f]);
const mismatches = enforced
.filter((f) => normalize(submitted[f]) !== normalize(document[f]!))
.map((f) => ({ field: f, submitted: submitted[f], document: document[f]! }));
return { ok: mismatches.length === 0, enforced, mismatches };

BirthInfoVerifier.verify.summary: Checks a KYC submission against the identity document: ok only if every part the document has (country, place) matches, ignoring case and surrounding spaces. A part the document lacks isn't checked; with no document at all, anything passes. Returns the mismatches for the error message.

BirthInfoService.get.name: get
BirthInfoService.get.summary: The user's birth info as one answer: what the identity document says and what they last submitted in KYC (with when), either of which may be missing. Reads both tables.

BirthInfoService.updateKycBirthInfo.name: updateKycBirthInfo
BirthInfoService.updateKycBirthInfo.summary: Saves what the user submitted as their KYC birth info, replacing what they submitted before. It must agree with their identity document: each part the document has is enforced, a missing part isn't.

diff.text: async updateKycBirthInfo(userId: string, dto: KycBirthInfoDto): Promise<BirthInfoView> {
await this.kyc.save(userId, { countryOfBirth: dto.countryOfBirth.trim().toUpperCase(), placeOfBirth: dto.placeOfBirth.trim() });
this.events.emit('kyc.birth_info.updated', { userId });
const submitted = { countryOfBirth: dto.countryOfBirth.trim().toUpperCase(), placeOfBirth: dto.placeOfBirth.trim() };
const document = await this.documents.forUser(userId);
const check = this.verifier.verify(submitted, document);
if (!check.ok) {
throw new UnprocessableEntityException({ message: 'Birth info does not match the identity document', mismatches: check.mismatches });
// The new answer and its event go together: if either fails, neither happens.
await this.dataSource.transaction(async (manager) => {
await this.kyc.save(userId, submitted, manager);
this.events.emit('kyc.birth_info.updated', { userId });
return this.get(userId);
